leftEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
leftEvidence.title: The faithful witness who freed by his blood

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: John greets the assemblies with grace and peace, names Jesus as faithful witness and firstborn from the dead, speaks of love and release from sins by blood, and announces his coming.
points.right: A Lamb stands as though slain between throne, living creatures, and elders, then takes the scroll.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: The Lamb’s standing life and visible slaughter are held together without turning the vision into a second Gospel scene.

payload.posture: Revelation names blood and death-memory in both an opening greeting and a throne vision.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: A standing Lamb appears slain

payload.tension: The opening names faithful witness, firstborn, ruler, love, release, and coming; the vision presents a standing slain Lamb, scroll, worship, purchased peoples, and kingdom.
payload.title: Witness who freed / Lamb who purchased
